text:
mira: Hey team, CI evals are showing nondeterministic outputs for the new quantized-2.1 model. Same seed + same prompt, different completions across runs. Not a flaky test — reproduces locally and in CI.

aj: ugh. Do we have per-worker seed logs? Could be worker resume or rng state not persisted.

mira: I dug into the logs. The eval runner prints a seed at start, but when a job resumes (checkpoint resume) it doesn't log the per-shard rng offset. Sample snippet:

```
[runner] seed=190238475
... processing batch 42
[worker-3] using stream_offset=0
[worker-3] done
```

next run output (different):
```
[runner] seed=190238475
[worker-3] using stream_offset=128
```

No codepath seems to set stream_offset when resuming.

seb: Tokenization drift could also cause different sampling behavior with top_p/temperature; quantized model uses a slightly different tokenizer version in the packaging step last week — did we pin tokenizer?

mira: I checked — packaging script uses `tokenizer_v: latest` for quant-2.1. We should've pinned. But the diffs in tokens are tiny (off by 1 token in ~0.5% samples) and wouldn't explain big semantic differences for low-temp runs.

aj: Can you paste a minimally repro command? I'll try to reproduce with a single-worker local runner.

mira: repro:
```
export SEED=190238475
python eval_runner.py --model quant-2.1 --prompt-file tests/short_prompts.jsonl --num-samples 3 --batch-size 1
```
Run twice back-to-back and compare outputs. On my machine, run A vs run B differ on sample 2 for prompt id 7.

runner-bot: CI job #4821 finished: eval-quant-2.1 (flaky) — logs: https://ci.example/c/4821

aj: okay reproduced locally. I instrumented RNG counters: looks like when resuming from checkpoint we don't advance per-shard RNG by the number of tokens emitted before the checkpoint. So resumed worker starts sampling with streams that overlap previous run. That explains nondeterminism.

seb: I also found tokenizer mismatch in the packaging CR: `tokenizer.json` in /packages/quant-2.1 was regenerated with SentencePiece v0.1.98 instead of v0.1.95 we normally use. I'll open a follow-up to pin that.

aj: quick patch: ensure runner persists `rng_state` in the checkpoint and applies `rng.advance(n)` for tokens already generated on resume. Patch snippet:
```
# on checkpoint save
checkpoint['rng_state'] = rng.serialize()
# on resume
rng.deserialize(checkpoint['rng_state'])
rng.advance(tokens_already_generated)
```
I'll open a PR.

mira: nice. Can we also add a CI test that repeatedly runs the same seed across resume boundaries? e.g., run, checkpoint halfway, resume, assert outputs equal to non-resumed run.

aj: yes — add a small smoke test in `eval-runner-smoke` with `--always-checkpoint`. Keep it small so it runs in CI.

infra-ci: Scheduling nightly canary job: `eval-resume-repro` on the dedicated pool at 03:30 UTC. Will also attach job artifacts to the eval dashboard.

mira: For observability, let's add a metric `rng.stream_overlap_count` whenever `rng.advance` is called with a negative/invalid offset (should never happen). Also tag runs where tokenizer version != pinned version.

seb: I'll send a packaging rollback for tokenizer to v0.1.95 for quant-2.1 ASAP.

aj: PR opened: https://git.example/runner/merge_requests/314 — fixes checkpoint rng serialization + adds smoke test.

mira: Thanks. Plan: merge hotfix -> run canary -> if clean, roll out to main CI. I'll attach example diffs and the discrepant output pairs to the ticket.

aj: small note: top_p sampling uses a cumulative probabilistic cutoff. If tokens are slightly different because of tokenizer change, top_p thresholding can pick a different token earlier, so both fixes are needed (rng persistence + tokenizer pin).

mira: agreed. Putting both in the rollout. Thanks all :thumbsup:

seb: I'll also add a changelog entry for packaging.

runner-bot: MR 314 pipeline passed minimal tests.

mira: closing loop — after hotfix landed, I reran the exact repro 5x and got identical outputs each time. Will watch canary.
